If I could change one thing about iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I'd get rid of the new top-down swipe gesture to invoke Siri AI. There are already plenty of ways to summon Siri, and I've always been used to swiping down on iPhone and iPad to open Notification Center, so this new gesture doesn't really affect my habits.

On the Mac side, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Even though it's already late August, new beta versions are still adding plenty of welcome changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's still one more change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes it harder to see the battery percentage on MacBook

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery controls in the menu bar. By default, only the battery icon is shown, not the percentage.

At first glance, this doesn't seem like a problem. I've even turned off the percentage display on my iPhone myself — the iPhone also uses a similar battery icon. However, I've always really liked being able to see the percentage on my Mac.

If you enable the "Show Percentage" option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the number is placed inside the battery icon. I assume Apple wanted to keep the design consistent with the iPhone in iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the iPhone's battery icon was a compromise Apple made to cope with the limited space to the right of the "M-notch" or Dynamic Island. But on the Mac, even in the menu bar, I've never run into a situation where there isn't enough screen space.

Since the first developer beta, I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air. I've found that because it's harder to read, I check the battery percentage less often overall.

I hope Apple will reconsider this in future design decisions, especially if more users find this design problematic. Until then, I've at least found a workaround myself.

I used Codex to write a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays battery status and percentage to suit my own needs. If you find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
